encounters.cc: Lower back pain radiating down posterior thighs for 6 months, worse with walking and standing

lines: Lower back pain radiating down posterior thighs for 6 months, worse with walking and standing
He presents to the clinic with a 6-month history of lower back pain that radiates down the posterior aspect of both thighs.
He reports that the pain is exacerbated by walking and standing for prolonged periods.
He finds some relief when he sits or leans forward while shopping with a cart.
- Chronic Heart Failure with reduced ejection fraction
- History of ischemic stroke with mild residual left-sided weakness
His past medical history includes hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Percutaneous coronary intervention (drug-eluting stent) to LAD
- Father: Myocardial infarction at age 62, hypertension
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, stroke at age 70
- No family history of amyloidosis or autoimmune disease
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Abstinent (formerly occasional). Occupation: Retired accountant.
On physical examination, there is no loss of lower extremity strength, and peripheral pulses are intact.
Straight leg raise test is negative bilaterally.
An MRI of the lumbar spine reveals narrowing of the spinal canal with associated degenerative changes in the facet joints and hypertrophy of the ligamentum flavum.

encounters.cc: Increasing fatigue, dyspnea on exertion, and bilateral lower extremity swelling over two months

lines: Increasing fatigue, dyspnea on exertion, and bilateral lower extremity swelling over two months
This 68-year-old male with systemic AL amyloidosis and chronic heart failure presents three months after Neurology evaluation for thoracic spinal stenosis.
He reports increasing fatigue, dyspnea on exertion, and bilateral lower extremity swelling over two months.
He denies chest pain, palpitations, or syncope.
- Chronic Heart Failure with reduced ejection fraction
- History of ischemic stroke with mild residual left-sided weakness
- Percutaneous coronary intervention (drug-eluting stent) to LAD
His medications include lisinopril, amlodipine, and furosemide.
- Father: Myocardial infarction at age 62, hypertension
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, stroke at age 70
- No family history of amyloidosis or autoimmune disease
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Abstinent (formerly occasional). Occupation: Retired accountant.
On physical examination, his blood pressure is 150/90 mmHg, heart rate is 88 beats per minute, and respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute.
Cardiac auscultation reveals a low-pitched diastolic rumble at the apex.
There is 2+ pitting edema up to the mid-shins bilaterally.
- Urinalysis: Proteinuria, no hematuria or casts
An echocardiogram shows increased ventricular wall thickness with normal chamber size and impaired diastolic filling without significant valvular abnormalities.

encounters.cc: Difficulty swallowing with coughing and choking, especially with liquids, over six months

lines: Difficulty swallowing with coughing and choking, especially with liquids, over six months

The patient is a 68-year-old male with systemic AL amyloidosis and thoracic spinal stenosis, recently evaluated by Cardiology and Neurology, who presents to Gastroenterology with a 6-month history of difficulty swallowing, which he describes as a problem initiating swallows.
He reports frequent coughing and choking when eating, especially with liquids.
He also mentions occasional nasal regurgitation.
- Chronic Heart Failure with reduced ejection fraction
- History of ischemic stroke with mild residual left-sided weakness
His past medical history includes poorly controlled diabetes mellitus type 2, hypertension, and a recent stroke with mild residual left-sided weakness.
- Percutaneous coronary intervention (drug-eluting stent) to LAD
- Father: Myocardial infarction at age 62, hypertension
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, stroke at age 70
- No family history of amyloidosis or autoimmune disease
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Abstinent (formerly occasional). Occupation: Retired accountant.
On physical examination, there is a slight slurring of speech and reduced gag reflex.
A videofluoroscopic modified barium swallow study shows delayed swallow initiation, pooling of contrast in the valleculae, and penetration of contrast into the laryngeal vestibule without aspiration.

encounters.cc: Two-month history of difficulty rising from chairs and climbing stairs with progressive fatigue

lines: Two-month history of difficulty rising from chairs and climbing stairs with progressive fatigue
The patient with AL amyloidosis and prior dyspnea evaluations presents with two-month difficulty rising from chairs and climbing stairs.
He denies recent trauma but reports increased fatigue and occasional exertional dyspnea.
- Chronic Heart Failure with reduced ejection fraction
- History of ischemic stroke with mild residual left-sided weakness
Medical history is significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension, both well controlled.
- Percutaneous coronary intervention (drug-eluting stent) to LAD
- Father: Myocardial infarction at age 62, hypertension
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, stroke at age 70
- No family history of amyloidosis or autoimmune disease
He does not use tobacco, alcohol, or illicit drugs.
Physical examination shows symmetric weakness in the deltoid, biceps, and quadriceps muscles bilaterally.
There is no rash, sensory loss, or joint swelling.
Laboratory results show a creatine kinase level of 3,200 U/L (normal: 22–198), and erythrocyte sedimentation rate is 72 mm/hr.

lines: Two-day history of progressive shortness of breath and bilateral ankle swelling with recent severe chest pain
Patient with systemic AL amyloidosis and chronic heart failure returns to the emergency department.
He reports a recent episode of severe chest pain that resolved spontaneously.
- Chronic Heart Failure with reduced ejection fraction
- History of ischemic stroke with mild residual left-sided weakness
- Percutaneous coronary intervention (drug-eluting stent) to LAD
- Father: Myocardial infarction at age 62, hypertension
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, stroke at age 70
- No family history of amyloidosis or autoimmune disease
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Abstinent (formerly occasional). Occupation: Retired accountant.

He has jugular venous distension, crackles at the lung bases, and 2+ pitting edema in both ankles.
An ECG shows ST-segment depressions in the anterior leads.

encounters.cc: Three-month history of progressive exertional dyspnea and bilateral ankle swelling

lines: Three-month history of progressive exertional dyspnea and bilateral ankle swelling
The patient with systemic AL amyloidosis and chronic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction returns for evaluation of recurrent symptoms.
He presents with a 3-month history of progressive exertional dyspnea and bilateral ankle swelling.
- Chronic Heart Failure with reduced ejection fraction
- History of ischemic stroke with mild residual left-sided weakness
He has a past medical history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Percutaneous coronary intervention (drug-eluting stent) to LAD
His medications include metformin, lisinopril, and hydrochlorothiazide.
- Father: Myocardial infarction at age 62, hypertension
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, stroke at age 70
- No family history of amyloidosis or autoimmune disease
He does not smoke and consumes alcohol occasionally.
On physical examination, his blood pressure is 145/90 mmHg, heart rate is 88 beats per minute, and respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute.
He has jugular venous distension, crackles at the lung bases, and 2+ pitting edema in both ankles.
His heart sounds include a third heart sound (S3).
Chest X-ray shows cardiomegaly and pulmonary congestion.

encounters.cc: Acute increasing shortness of breath over two days with orthopnea requiring three pillows

lines: Acute increasing shortness of breath over two days with orthopnea requiring three pillows
This 73-year-old with AL amyloidosis and heart failure returns with symptoms similar to one year prior.
He reports needing 3 pillows to sleep comfortably and has had difficulty walking more than a block due to fatigue and breathlessness.
He has not had chest pain, fever, or recent illness.
- Chronic Heart Failure with reduced ejection fraction
- History of ischemic stroke with mild residual left-sided weakness
- Percutaneous coronary intervention (drug-eluting stent) to LAD
He takes lisinopril, amlodipine, and metformin.
- Father: Myocardial infarction at age 62, hypertension
- Mother: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, stroke at age 70
- No family history of amyloidosis or autoimmune disease
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Abstinent (formerly occasional). Occupation: Retired accountant.
Temperature is 36.8°C (98.2°F), blood pressure is 155/95 mm Hg, pulse is 95/min, and respirations are 22/min.
Pulse oximetry shows 93% on room air.
Cardiac auscultation reveals a normal S1 and S2 with a third heart sound (S3).
Bibasilar crackles are heard on lung auscultation, and there is jugular venous distension but no peripheral edema.
Fundoscopy reveals arteriolar narrowing without papilledema.
